name: Vi
description: Voice set for Officer Vi (skin 2): a lone-wolf patrol cop who has burned through every partner in the department, until a sharpshooting one finally kept up. Squad cars, sirens, tickets, the bullpen's betting pool and a partner she pretends not to like. Builds on vi-original.json.

messages.message: {momentTitle} is {voteDiff} down. That's a pile-up. Get the sirens going.
Thirty or more behind. Radio every unit you know. Lights and sirens.
{momentTitle} is {voteDiff} behind. Knock on doors. Somebody's sitting on a vote.
Fifteen-odd behind. Fender bender, not a wreck.
Down {voteDiff}. Time to get a partner. I know, I know, I'm the worst at that.
{voteDiff} behind. A couple of pull-overs and we're level.
Down {voteDiff}. Minor ticket. Pay it off before the bell.
Dead level. One vote tips it. Floor the cruiser.
One vote apart. No more waiting in the parking lot.
{voteDiff} votes between them. Photo finish. Get more cars on the road.
{voteDiff} votes apart. Chase goes all the way to the line.
{momentTitle} is sitting on {userPct}%. Clear road ahead.
{userPct}% and still rolling. Don't ease off the gas.
{userPct}%. Solid lead. Eyes on the mirrors.
{userPct}% on your pick. We're out front. Keep the lights on.
Up at {userPct}%. Good. Cruise control is for rookies, though.
{momentTitle} was {voteDiff} down and just took the lead. Best bet the bullpen never made.
{voteDiff} behind, now ahead. The late votes came screaming in with sirens on.
Climbed out of a {voteDiff} hole. Somebody owes somebody twenty bucks.
{momentTitle} was losing. Plot twist.
{momentTitle} just pulled ahead. Called it. Okay, I bet against it. Don't tell anyone.

messages: {username} voted with you on {momentTitle}. Two officers, one call.
{username} picked {momentTitle} too. Partners already, apparently.
{username} agrees with you. Mark it in the logbook.
Same pick as {username}. Squad car's getting crowded.
{username} backed {momentTitle}. Good instincts for a civilian.
{username} went with the same one. Ride-along approved.
{username} is riding with you on {momentTitle}. Keep them close.
{username} made the same call. Nobody's arguing.
{username} voted {momentTitle}. Welcome to the bullpen.
{username} voted {theirMoment} against {yourMoment}. Wrong turn.
{username} picked {theirMoment}. Let's see who gets the ticket.
{username} went the other way on {yourMoment}. Wrong, but gutsy.
{username} voted against you. I'd argue, but the tally writes better reports.
{username} took {theirMoment}. Cocky. Dumb, but cocky.
{username} is against {yourMoment}. Fine. Pull over and let's talk.
{username} disagrees on {yourMoment}. Let the votes hand out the citation.
{username} voted the other way. They'll be begging for a warning.
details: Everyone runs a red light sometimes.
Don't take it personal. Or take it as a challenge.
A rival keeps the lone wolf sharp.
They'll come around when the sirens stop.
At least it's a fair chase.

messages: Ten in a row with {username}. That's not luck, that's a real partnership.
{username} and you, ten matches, same call every time. The bullpen is jealous.
Ten straight with {username}. Best partner streak I've seen. Me included.
A ten-match run with {username}. Smooth driving.
Ten for ten with {username}. Impressive. Keep it out of the break room.
{streakCount} matches with {username}. That's past partners, that's a whole squad.
{streakCount} in a row with {username}. I'd ride shotgun with you two anywhere.
{streakCount} straight picks with {username}. Outrageous. In the best way.
A {streakCount}-match run with {username}. Nobody's beating that record.
{streakCount} with {username}. Hand over the keys to the department.
Ten matches against {username}. That's an official feud.
{username} has gone against you ten times running. They hate your driving.
Ten in a row opposite {username}. Neither of you is pulling over.
A ten-match run against {username}. Two stubborn officers, one stalemate.
Ten times at odds with {username}. I'd put money on it. Wait, we already did.
details: Talk it out. Or race it out.

messages: {streakCount} against {username}. That's not a rivalry, that's a turf war on wheels.
{streakCount} in a row opposite {username}. Neither of you gives up the road.
{streakCount} straight disagreements with {username}. Stubborn is too small a word.
A {streakCount}-match feud with {username}. Somebody call the sergeant.
{streakCount} against {username}. I respect it. Take a day off, though.
details: Glad I'm not riding in the middle.

messages: {matchTitle} wraps in {timeLeft} and you're still idling at the curb. Move.
{timeLeft} left on {matchTitle}. Your vote's not in the logbook. Fix that.
{matchTitle} wraps in {timeLeft}. Your vote's the one overdue.
{timeLeft} left on {matchTitle}. Lights and sirens.
{matchTitle} closes in {timeLeft}. Don't make me come write you up.
Only {timeLeft} until {matchTitle} ends. Your log is still blank.
{matchTitle} closes in {timeLeft}. Last lap.
{timeLeft} left. Decide. Go.
Final call on {matchTitle}. {timeLeft}. Floor it.
{matchCount} matches you haven't voted in are about to close. The first one wraps in {timeLeft}.
{matchCount} unvoted matches against the clock. The nearest ends in {timeLeft}.
No votes on {matchTitle}. Somebody hit the sirens first.
{moment1} against {moment2} and no votes at all. I'll idle here. For a bit.
New match, zero votes. Be the first car on the scene.
{matchTitle} is empty. Roll up and take it.
{totalVotes} vote{votesPlural}. That's a quiet road.
Hardly a car on this road. Send some traffic.
Turnout's low. Come on, give me some traffic.
Nobody's pulled up on this one. Somebody should.
details: When the road is this empty, every vote is a headlight.

messages: {matchTitle} is deadlocked and you haven't voted. Break it up.
Dead level on {matchTitle}. One vote makes the call.
Tied. Someone has to take the lead. Make it you.
{moment1} and {moment2}, bumper to bumper. Pick one.
Still tied and almost out of road. Last chance to break it.
Level and the clock's winding down. Vote.
Tied, and nearly out of time. Don't idle this one out.
Round {round} is open. {matchCount} new matches. Start your engine.
{matchCount} matches just opened in round {round}. Roll call.
Round {round} is live, {matchCount} matches on the road.
New round. {matchCount} matches. Pick your route.
Round {round}: {matchCount} matches idling for your call.
{momentTitle} won. Paid up and proud.
{momentTitle} is through. Good call, officer.
{momentTitle} took it. Clean getaway.
{momentTitle} won, and it earned the win.
{momentTitle} advances. Easy ride.
{momentTitle} moves on. That's how a pro drives.
details: That's a win for the logbook.

messages: {momentTitle} lost. That one smarts.
{momentTitle} is out. Not the ruling I wanted.
{momentTitle} didn't make it. Walk it off.
{momentTitle} went down swinging. Good effort.
{momentTitle} is out. Back in the car.
{momentTitle} lost this round. Annoying. We'll tail the next one.
{momentTitle} got knocked out. We take the next stop.
details: Another call is always coming in.

messages: Still deciding? Quit idling and pick.
Don't overthink it. Make the call and roll.
They've all earned a glance. Trust your gut.
You've sat at that stoplight long enough. Pick.
details: No wrong way to pick. Plenty of tickets, though.

messages: Welcome to the squad. {liveCount} matches are open. Pick one.
New recruit? {liveCount} matches are live. Hop in.
Good timing. {liveCount} matches are waiting on votes.
{liveCount} matches open. Choose a side of the street.
Welcome. {liveCount} matches. Let's see how you drive, rookie.
Day two. You came back for the ride. Good.
Two days running. Nice.
Back for day two. I noticed.
{days} days gone. Nice of you to roll up.
After {days} days you're back. The department kept your seat warm.
{days} days. Thought you'd transferred. Glad you didn't.
{days} days away. A lot of calls piled up.
You're back in the squad car. Good.
Welcome back. Let's roll.
Back already. Nice.
Hey. The calls are coming in.
First vote logged. Welcome aboard, rookie.
You picked a side. First ticket written.
Five votes. The engine's warming up.
Five. You've moved past civilian.
Ten votes. The bullpen knows your name.
Ten. You've got your own parking spot now.
details: Regulars hold the department together. +{xp} XP

messages: Twenty-five votes. You're a voice on the radio now.
Twenty-five. The whole bullpen listens.
Fifty votes. You're deep in the logbooks.
Fifty. You genuinely care. Impressive.
A hundred votes. They'll name a squad car after you.
One hundred. Genuinely impressive. Don't tell the sergeant.
Three days running. That's a routine.
Three days running. You're dependable.
details: Showing up is the hard part. +{xp} XP
Three days on the road. +{xp} XP

messages: A whole week on the road. That's real dedication.
Seven days in a row. Respect.
details: A week without a sick day. +{xp} XP

messages: Two weeks. You never clock out early, do you?
Fourteen days straight. That's wild.
details: Two weeks, not one day missed. +{xp} XP

messages: Thirty days. Truthfully? Thanks for staying on the force.
A month of clocking in. That means a lot to this department.
details: Thirty days on the road. +{xp} XP
A full month in the squad car. +{xp} XP

messages: Five underdogs. You back the ones nobody bets on.
Five long shots. Lone wolf energy. I like it.
details: Five and still your own officer. +{xp} XP

messages: Fifteen underdogs. You pick the hard calls on purpose.
Fifteen. You never follow the pack.
details: Every call is yours alone. +{xp} XP
Fifteen votes for the long shot. +{xp} XP

messages: Thirty underdogs. Nobody in the bullpen can read you.
Thirty. The long shot is your trademark.
details: Nobody knows your next move. +{xp} XP
Thirty votes for whoever was trailing. +{xp} XP

messages: First on scene five times. You don't wait for backup.
Five times you got to the scene first.
details: You arrive before the sirens. +{xp} XP
Five votes before the traffic. +{xp} XP

messages: Fifteen matches with you leading the convoy. Habit forming.
First car on the scene, again and again.
details: Fifteen first arrivals on scene. +{xp} XP
Ahead of the whole department. +{xp} XP

messages: Ten close matches. Photo finishes are your thing.
Another squeaker. Your nerves are better than mine.
Twenty-five close matches. Your vote keeps winning the chase.
You've settled it more than once.
You stuck with the underdog five times. Stubborn. I approve.
You don't dump the side that's losing. Respect.
details: Five rallies you stood by. +{xp} XP

messages: Same moment, three times. Somebody's got a favourite perp.
That one again? Must be good.
Five votes, one moment. That's partner-level loyalty.
You're not pulling away from that one. Fine by me.
details: One favourite, five votes logged. +{xp} XP

messages: Ten votes on the same moment. That's an obsession, officer.
Ten times, same pick. Not writing you up. Yet.
Two rounds. You're sticking with the ride.
Round two and you're still in the car. Good.
details: Stay for the next stop. +{xp} XP

messages: Four rounds. You're deep in the chase.
Deep in the bracket. The real pursuits start now.
details: A long way from the first call. +{xp} XP

messages: Six rounds. You rode it all the way.
All the way. You didn't bail at the last stop.
Ten matches. You check every side street.
Ten different matches. Thorough. Good officer.
Twenty-five matches. You've covered every district.
Twenty-five. No corner left unvisited.
Fifty matches. That's not browsing, that's a pension.
Fifty. You know this bracket like your own patrol route.
Five in one sitting. Decent speed.
Five back to back. Keep driving.
Ten in one go. Grab a coffee.
Ten in one sitting. Overtime stamina.
Voting at this hour? Graveyard run or insomnia?
Dead of night. Dedication, or the coffee's too strong.
details: The graveyard run suits you. +{xp} XP

messages: You spread the word. Thanks, partner.
Five shares. More cars on the road, more votes.
details: Cheers for the radio calls. +{xp} XP

messages: Fifteen shares. They should hand you a uniform.
Fifteen. You keep recruiting. Love it.
You were here before the department opened. Founding member, for good.
One of the first thousand. Nobody takes that off you.
details: That title stays with you for the whole career. +{xp} XP

messages: New rank. Earned out on the road.
Promoted. Try not to let the cap go to your head.
Achievement unlocked: {name}. Good work, officer.
Another one in the logbook: {name}.
{rank}. Hard-earned.
You put the miles in and it shows.
Ten underdogs. Reckless. It's a family trait, sadly.
Ten long shots. You barely blink.
details: Ten against the bullpen's odds. +{xp} XP
Long shots are your speciality, officer. +{xp} XP

messages: Ten close ones with Cait. Your nerves are steel. Mine too, mostly.
Ten tight finishes. She'd be proud. I might be too.
Seven days with Cait. Best partner I ever had. Don't repeat that.
A week without a slip. Nice driving.
details: A week at her side. +{xp} XP
Seven days on the road. +{xp} XP

messages: You broke the tie. Neat stop.
Tied match, and you made the stop. Respect.
details: The vote that made the arrest. +{xp} XP

messages: Officer Vi, reporting. I've got your back.
Vi's your partner now. Try not to ruin it. I will, but try.

upcoming: Not open yet. Wait in the car.
Voting hasn't started. I'll hit the sirens when it does.
prevote: Two edits, one vote. Watch both, then make the call.
Watch them both before you choose. No snap judgments.
I'm not giving you the answer. Your stop.
Take a minute. Then write it up.
Go with your gut. It's seldom wrong.
prevote-empty: No votes yet. Be the first car on scene.
Quiet road. Somebody start the traffic.
Blank so far. Make the first entry in the logbook.
closing-24h: Under a day left and no vote from you. Climb in.
The garage door's closing. Pick now.
closing-3h: Time's short. Vote before the lot closes.
voted-early: You voted early with barely anyone in. First car there.
Hardly a vote in and you picked. Decisive.
voted-ahead: Your pick's ahead. Nice. Chase isn't over.
A lead's a lead. Check the mirrors.
voted-close: That's close. Too close. I'm chewing my badge strap.
Razor margin. One vote flips the ruling. Radio somebody.
Bumper to bumper. Your pick needs backup.
{pct} to {otherPct}. Keep your eyes on the road.
voted-tied: Dead level. Neither car has the lead.
A perfect tie. Maddening. Somehow lovely.
voted-behind: You're behind. That doesn't make you the suspect.
{pick} is trailing. Underdog. My favourite kind of suspect.
They're ahead. You're not wrong, just short on backup.
Down by {diff} points. Tell people. Call it in.
Most went the other way. That proves nothing.
closed-won: {pick} went through. You read the road right.
closed-lost: Your pick lost. It smarts. Brush it off.
It didn't make it. Happens. Next stop.
{pick} is out. Tough break. It was a solid pick.
closed-tied: A tie. Neither side would pull over.
closed-unvoted: The vote closed and you missed it. More are rolling in.
Match is over. {winner} took it. Next time, get in the car.

first-vote: First vote. Welcome. Every officer writes a first ticket.
That's your first one. Paperwork gets easier.
streak: {streak} days in a row. I see you in the squad car.
underdog: You backed the one nobody else would. Noted.
An underdog pick. Takes a lot of nerve.
early: Early. You beat the crowd to the scene.
Few votes so far. Yours is a loud siren.
close: That vote bumped the margin. It's tight.
Razor thin. One more voter tips it.
Close call. Your vote counts double.
behind: {pick} is behind. Behind isn't busted. Bring people.
Not winning yet. Time to call in the extra units.
ahead: {pick} is ahead. Don't coast. Leads slip.
Looks like a good stop from here.
default: Noted. I'm not arguing it. For now.
Vote's logged. Plenty more to see.

live-fresh: {unvoted} matches and no sides picked. Start with the one you've got a hunch about.
All routes are open. Choose. I won't tailgate you.
{unvoted} to go. No pressure. Maybe a little siren pressure.
live-some: {voted} done, {unvoted} to go. Keep the engine running.
You're off the lot. {unvoted} more waiting.
Good start. The rest won't clear themselves.
live-few: Only {unvoted} left. Finish the route today.
live-one: Last stop. Don't leave it hanging.
One match between you and the parking lot.
live-closing: Some of these close in {timeLeft}. {unvoted} still need your vote.
The clock's running. {unvoted} left, {timeLeft} to go.
Almost out of time. Floor it.
live-done: You've voted in everything. Nice driving. Go check the bracket.
Nothing left on your route. Come back when the next round opens.
live-none: Nothing's live right now. New calls will come in. Study the bracket meanwhile.
No matches open. Even the radio's quiet.
brackets-groups: Groups first. Top two from each go through. The rest get towed.
Everyone begins in a group. Not everyone drives out.
Watch the tables. They shift fast.
brackets-knockout-soon: Knockouts ahead. The top two in each group get through.
No knockout yet. The groups need to finish their laps.
Patience. The knockout sets up once the groups wrap.
brackets-knockout-live: Knockouts now. Lose once and you're out of the race.
Every match carries more weight now. Pick with care.
brackets-bracket: Round by round. One bad turn and you're towed.
Follow the bracket. The road narrows every round.
Every line here is a stop somebody voted on.
brackets-complete: That's the cup done. Thanks for riding with me.
It's over. Good run. I'll miss the sirens.
We've got a champion. Worth the ride.
brackets-empty: No bracket yet. Nobody's been called in.
Empty board. The draw's still on its way. Soon.
Nothing logged yet. Check back later.

invite: {a} or {b}. One vote could turn it. Make the stop.
Two edits, one pick: {a} against {b}. Cast your vote.
{a} versus {b}. Hop in and tell me what you think.
voted: I voted {pick} over {other}. What's your ruling?
{pick} gets my vote over {other}. Fight me on it.
I went with {pick} over {other}. Want to pull me over?
early: One of the first votes on {pick} against {other}. We need more cars on the road.
First car there for {pick} over {other}. Add yours.
{pick} versus {other}, hardly a vote yet. Yours would count double.
tied: {pick} and {other} are dead level. One vote closes the file.
A tie, {pick} against {other}. Somebody make the stop.
{pick} and {other} are glued together. Your vote can pry them apart.
nailbiter: {pick} and {other} are {voteDiff} votes apart. Every vote's a flashing light now.
Just {voteDiff} votes between {pick} and {other}. Hit yours.
{pick} against {other}, {voteDiff} apart. The road could fork either way.
losing-close: {pick} is {voteDiff} behind {other}. A few votes change lanes.
Down {voteDiff} to {other}, but {pick} can still take the chase. Go help.
{pick} trails {other} by {voteDiff}. Easy to close. Vote.
losing-bad: {pick} is {voteDiff} behind {other}. It needs a second unit.
Down {voteDiff} to {other}. {pick} deserves a smoother ride. Vote.
{pick} is getting outrun by {other}, {voteDiff} down. Let's close the gap.
winning-close: {pick} leads {other} at {pct}%, barely. Help it keep the lane.
{pick} leads {other} at {pct}%. It's no lock yet. Vote.
{pct}% for {pick} over {other}. A narrow lead. For now.
dominating: {pick} is out front of {other} at {pct}%. Come see the chase.
{pct}% for {pick}. {other} is a tail light in the distance.
{pick} leads {other} by a mile, {pct}%. Add to the lead.
